claims.text: Eligibility: you must graduate from an entry-level PA program accredited by ARC-PA to take PANCE.
claims.quote: To be eligible for PANCE, you must graduate from an entry-level PA program accredited by ARC-PA.
claims.locator: Who is eligible to apply for PANCE?

claims.text: Six years, six attempts: for first-time candidates, after graduating you can take PANCE for up to six years, at most six times; once either runs out, eligibility is lost and the only way back is to complete an accredited PA program again.
claims.quote: Individuals who have never been certified and who graduated from an ARC-PA accredited PA program on or after January 1, 2003, will be eligible to take PANCE for up to six years after completing the requirements for graduation from that program. During that six-year period, PANCE may be taken a total of six times. When either the six attempts or six years are exhausted, whichever occurs sooner, the individual loses eligibility to take PANCE. The only way to establish new eligibility is to complete an unabridged ARC-PA accredited PA educational program again.
claims.locator: Limitations on eligibility: the six-years-six-attempts rule

claims.text: The exam: five blocks of 60 questions, 60 minutes per block; 45 minutes of break time in total, plus a 15-minute tutorial.
claims.quote: PANCE consists of five blocks of 60 questions with 60 minutes to complete each block. There is a total of 45 minutes allotted for breaks between blocks and 15 minutes to view a tutorial.

claims.text: PA-C: after passing PANCE you are NCCPA board certified and may use the legally protected PA-C mark for as long as your certification stays current.
claims.quote: After passing PANCE, PAs are issued NCCPA board certification and can use the legally protected marks, PA-C® or Physician Assistant-Certified® as long as they maintain a current certification status.

claims.text: Licensure depends on it: all 50 states, DC, the US territories and the military rely on NCCPA certification as one of the criteria for employment, licensure or regulation of PAs.
claims.quote: All 50 states, the District of Columbia, the U.S. Territories, the U.S. military, and many employers have decided to rely on NCCPA certification as one of the criteria for employment, licensure or regulation of PAs.

notes.issue: Claim dropped the source's qualifier (never-certified graduates of ARC-PA programs on or after January 1, 2003).
notes.resolution: Added 'for first-time candidates' and extended the quote to include the qualifier; re-check passed.
